name: Mary Maxwell Gates

summary.text: Mary Maxwell Gates (1929–1994) was a Seattle civic leader, University of Washington regent and the mother of Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates. She joined the national board of United Way in 1980 and in 1983 became the first woman to chair its national executive committee. IBM chief executive John Opel served with her on that board, and she is credited with helping cement Microsoft's early connection with IBM.

openQuestions: The site says she served on United Way's national executive committee 'alongside IBM chairman John Opel' in 1980; the obituary places both on the national board in 1980 and dates her executive-committee chairmanship to 1983. Broadly supported, with the timing nuance.
The site's claim that this relationship was the quid pro quo for IBM's choice of Microsoft is characterisation; the sources describe her as having 'helped cement' the connection.
